\section{Efficient computation of the SIDIS cross section}

In this section, we will manipulate the formulas for the SIDIS cross
section so to make them optimal from the point of view of the
implementation. The goal is to make their numerical computation as
efficient as possible. The SIDIS differential cross section for the
exchange of a virtual photon can be written as:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{d^3\sigma}{dx dQdz} = 
  \frac{4\pi\alpha^2}{Q^3} 
  \left[ \frac{Y_+}{x} F_2(x,z,Q^2)
    -\frac{y^2}{x} F_L(x,z,Q^2) \right]\,,
\label{eq:sidis2}
\end{equation}
where we have defined:
\begin{equation}
Y_+ = 1+(1-y)^2\,.
\end{equation}
The structure functions $F_2$ and $F_L$ are given at NLO by the
following convolution:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle  F(x,z,Q) &=& \displaystyle x\sum_{q\overline{q}} e_q^2 \bigg[ 
                                    \left(C_{qq}(x,z|Q) \otimes f_q(x|Q) +   
                                    C_{qg}(x,z|Q) \otimes f_g(x|Q)\right)\otimes d_q(z|Q) \\
                                &+&\displaystyle   \left(C_{gq}(x,z|Q) \otimes f_q(x|Q)\right)\otimes d_g(z|Q) \bigg]\,,
\end{array}
\label{eq:f1sidis}
\end {equation}
where $\{f_q,f_g\}$ are the quark and gluon PDFs and $\{d_q,d_g\}$ are
the quark and gluon FFs, $e_q$ is the electric charge of the quark $q$
and $\{C^{2,L}_{qq},C^{2,L}_{qg},C^{2,L}_{gq}\}$ are the relevant
partonic cross sections. Importantly, the perturbative coefficients of
the coefficient functions $C$ factorise as follows:
\begin{equation}
C(x,z) = \sum_t c_tO_t^{(1)}(x)O_t^{(2)}(z)\,,
\label{eq:decomposition}
\end{equation}
where $c_t$ are numerical coefficients, and $O_t^{(1)}$ and
$O_t^{(2)}$ are one-dimensional functions of $x$ and $z$,
respectively. Since we are interested in isolating the FFs at some
initial scale $Q_0$, we also write:
\begin{equation}
d_{q(g)}(z|Q) = T_{q(g)i}d_{i}(z|Q) = T_{q(g)i}\Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\otimes d_{j}(z|Q_0)\,,
\label{eq:rotationandevolution}
\end{equation}
where $\Gamma_{ij}$ is the appropriate evolution operator and
$T_{q(g)i}$ is the rotation matrix from the evolution to the physical
basis. Now, for the generic structure function, let us define:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
\mathbb{C}_{j}(z|x,Q,Q_0) &=&\displaystyle \bigg[C_{qq}(x,z|Q) \otimes \left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2 f_q(x|Q) T_{qi}\right) +
  \left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2 T_{qi}\right) C_{qg}(x,z|Q) \otimes f_g(x|Q) \\
\\
&+&\displaystyle C_{gq}(x,z|Q) \otimes
    \left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2f_q(x|Q)\right) T_{gi}\bigg]\otimes
    \Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\\
\\
&=&\mathbb{K}_i^{\rm SIDIS}(z|x,Q)\otimes \Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\,,
\end{array}
\label{eq:explicit}
\end{equation}
where we have used the fact that, in the zero-mass scheme, the quark
hard cross sections do not depend on the specific quark flavour, such
that:
\begin{equation}
  \displaystyle  F(x,z,Q) = \sum_j \mathbb{C}_{j}(z|x,Q,Q_0) \otimes d_{j}(z|Q_0)\,.
\end {equation}
Using the perturbative expansion of the hard cross sections and
Eq.~(\ref{eq:decomposition}), the factor $\mathbb{K}^{\rm SIDIS}$ in
Eq.~(\ref{eq:explicit}) can be written more explicitly as:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
\mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS}(z|x,Q) &=&  \displaystyle\left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2f_q(x|Q)T_{qi}\right)\delta(1-z)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle a_s(Q) \sum_t
      c_{qq,t}\left[O_{qq,t}^{(1)}\otimes \left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2 f_q(Q) T_{qi}\right)\right](x)O_{qq,t}^{(2)}(z)\\
  \\
                          &+&\displaystyle a_s(Q)\left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2T_{qi}\right)\sum_t c_{qg,t}\left[ O_{qg,t}^{(1)}\otimes f_g(Q) \right](x)O_{qg,t}^{(2)}(z)\\
  \\
                          &+&\displaystyle a_s(Q) T_{gi}\sum_t c_{gq,t}\left[ O_{gq,t}^{(1)}\otimes
                              \left(\sum_{q\overline{q}}e_q^2f_q(Q)\right) \right](x)O_{gq,t}^{(2)}(z)\,,
\end{array}
\end{equation}
with:
\begin{equation}
a_s(Q)=\frac{\alpha_s(Q)}{4\pi}\,.
\end{equation}
Note that, given the evolution and physical basis, one has that
$T_{gi}=\delta_{gi}$ and $T_{qg}=0$. Finally, defining:
\begin{equation}
\mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS}(z|x,Q) =   \frac{4\pi\alpha^2}{Q^3} 
  \left[ \frac{Y_+}{x} \mathbb{K}_{2,i}^{\rm SIDIS} (z|x,Q)
    -\frac{y^2}{x} \mathbb{K}_{L,i}^{\rm SIDIS} (z|x,Q)\right]\,,
\end{equation}
one has:
\begin{equation}
  \frac{d^3\sigma}{dx dQdz} = \sum_j
  \mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS} (z|x,Q)\otimes\Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\otimes
  d_{j}(z|Q_0)\,.
\label{eq:sidisInt}
\end{equation}

\subsection{NNLO expressions}

Extending the calculation of the SIDIS cross section to NNLO accuracy implies,
on top of the mere inclusion of the $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s^2)$ contribution to
the hard cross sections, a number of complications. First, the flavour structure
in Eq.~(\ref{eq:f1sidis}) becomes significantly more involved. Second, the
factorisation of the hard cross sections in terms of bi-linear operators in
Eq.~(\ref{eq:decomposition}) no longer holds. In this section, we will show how
to overcome these complications.

\subsubsection{Electromagnetic structure functions}

We use the notation of Refs.~\cite{Bonino:2024qbh, Bonino:2024wgg}
focusing on the flavour structure. Therefore, we neglect all
dependences and Mellin convolutions. Moreover, here we concentrate on
electromagnetic structure functions, \textit{i.e.} those structure
function characterised by the exchange of virtual photon. This has the
consequence that only electric charges will appear. The following
discussion is applicable to both unpolarised and polarised structure
functions, which, under the assumption of photon-exchange only, are
$F_2$ and $F_L$ in the unpolarised case, and $g_1$ in the polarised
case. With these premises, the structure of a SIDIS structure
functions to NNLO accuracy reads:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle F&=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{\rm NS}\left(\sum_{\alpha} e_\alpha^2f_\alpha d_\alpha\right)+C_{qg}f_g\left(\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha^2d_\alpha\right)+C_{gq} d_g\left(\sum_{\beta}e_\beta^2f_\beta\right)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{gg}\left(\sum_{\gamma}e_\gamma^2\right)f_gd_g+C_{qq}^{\rm PS}\left(\sum_{\gamma}e_\gamma^2\right)\left(\sum_{\alpha}f_\alpha d_\alpha\right)+C_{\overline{q}q}\left(\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha^2f_{-\alpha}d_\alpha\right)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(1)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\beta^2 f_\beta d_\alpha\right) +C_{q'q}^{(2)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\alpha^2 f_\beta d_\alpha\right) +C_{q'q}^{(3)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\alpha e_\beta f_\beta d_\alpha\right) \,,
  \end{array}
  \label{eq:emstructurefunctions}
\end{equation}
where the second and third lines only appear at NNLO. Moreover, the coefficient
functions $C$ can no longer be written as in Eq.~(\ref{eq:decomposition}). The
indices $\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$ run over all active quark flavours
\textit{and} anti-flavours, \textit{i.e.} they are indices in the physical
basis, and in principle also over the gluon. We now use
Eq.~(\ref{eq:rotationandevolution}) to rotate FFs from the physical to the
evolution basis and to introduce their evolution. We rewrite
Eq.~(\ref{eq:rotationandevolution}) as follows
\begin{equation}
  d_{\alpha} = T_{\alpha i}d_{i} = T_{\alpha i}\Gamma_{ij} d_{j}^{(0)}\,,
  \label{eq:rotationandevolution2}
\end{equation}
where we removed all dependences and convolution symbols and, with abuse of
notation, we indicated with $d_i$, or with any latin index, the $i$-th FF in the
evolution basis, while $d_{j}^{(0)}$ is the $j$-th FF in the evolution basis at
the initial scale $Q_0$. Also note that $T_{gi}=\delta_{gi}$ and
$T_{g\alpha}=\delta_{g\alpha}$. We now use this relation to replace all FFs in
the physical basis with their evolution basis counterparts. We then have:
\begin{equation}
F = \mathbb{K}_{i}\Gamma_{ij}d_{j}^{(0)}\,,
\end{equation}
where now:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle \mathbb{K}_{i}&=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{\rm NS}\left(\sum_{\alpha} e_\alpha^2f_\alpha T_{\alpha i}\right)+C_{qg}f_g\left(\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha^2 T_{\alpha i}\right)+C_{gq} T_{g i}\left(\sum_{\beta}e_\beta^2f_\beta\right)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{gg}\left(\sum_{\gamma}e_\gamma^2\right)f_gT_{g i}+C_{qq}^{\rm PS}\left(\sum_{\gamma}e_\gamma^2\right)\left(\sum_{\alpha}f_\alpha T_{\alpha i}\right)+C_{\overline{q}q}\left(\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha^2f_{-\alpha}T_{\alpha i}\right)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(1)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\beta^2 f_\beta T_{\alpha i}\right) +C_{q'q}^{(2)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\alpha^2 f_\beta T_{\alpha i}\right) +C_{q'q}^{(3)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\alpha e_\beta f_\beta T_{\alpha i} \right) \,,
  \end{array}
\end{equation}
where, importantly, greek indices ($\alpha$, $\beta$, and $\gamma$) only run
over active quarks and antiquarks and not over the gluon. Given the structure of
$T_{\alpha i}$, this has the consequence that if $i$ corresponds to the gluon
only the terms proportional to $C_{gq}$ and $C_{gg}$ survive. Conversely, if $i$
corresponds to any of the quark quark combinations, the terms proportional to
$C_{gq}$ and $C_{gg}$ drop while all others remain. Therefore, we could write:
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{K}_{g} = C_{gq} \left(\sum_{\beta}e_\beta^2f_\beta\right)+ C_{gg}\left(\sum_{\gamma}e_\gamma^2\right)f_g\,,
\end{equation}
while:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle \mathbb{K}_{i\neq g}&=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{\rm NS}\left(\sum_{\alpha} e_\alpha^2f_\alpha T_{\alpha i}\right)+C_{qg}f_g\left(\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha^2 T_{\alpha i}\right)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{\rm PS}\left(\sum_{\gamma}e_\gamma^2\right)\left(\sum_{\alpha}f_\alpha T_{\alpha i}\right)+C_{\overline{q}q}\left(\sum_{\alpha}e_\alpha^2f_{-\alpha}T_{\alpha i}\right)\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(1)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\beta^2 f_\beta T_{\alpha i}\right) +C_{q'q}^{(2)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\alpha^2 f_\beta T_{\alpha i}\right) +C_{q'q}^{(3)} \left(\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq \beta,-\beta}} e_\alpha e_\beta f_\beta T_{\alpha i} \right) \,.
  \end{array}
\end{equation}

Since this time it is convenient to parameterise the cross section in terms of
the structure functions $F_T$ and $F_L$, with $F_L=F_2-F_T$, we have that:
\begin{equation}
  \mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS}=\frac{8\pi\alpha^2}{Q^3}\left[ \frac{Y_+}{2x} \mathbb{K}_{T,i}+\frac{1-y}{x} \mathbb{K}_{L,i}\right]\,.
\end{equation}

\subsubsection{Electroweak structure functions}

In this section, we generalise the discussion of the previous section
by considering, on top of photon exchange, also $Z$ and $W$
exchange. This leads to several complications:
\begin{itemize}
\item The need to define neutral-current (NC) and charged-current (CC)
  structure functions characterised by the exchange of neutral
  $\gamma/Z$ boson and a $W$, respectively.
\item The introduction of $Q$-dependent vector and axial electroweak
  couplings,
\item The need to introduce, in the unpolarised case, the
  parity-violating structure function $F_3$.
\end{itemize}
In what follows, we will adhere to the notation of
Ref.~\cite{Bonino:2025qta}. We aim at computing the structure function
$\mathcal{F}_{i}^{jk}$, with $i=T,L,3$ and
$jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ,W^+,W^-$, such that we can define NC and
CC structure functions respectively as the following combinations:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{l}
    \displaystyle \mathcal{F}_{i}^{\rm NC}=\mathcal{F}_{i}^{\gamma\gamma}-g_V^\ell P_Z
    \mathcal{F}_{i}^{\gamma Z}+(g_V^{\ell2}+g_A^{\ell2})P_Z^2
    \mathcal{F}_{i}^{\gamma Z}\,,\quad i=T,L\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \mathcal{F}_{3}^{\rm
    NC}=-g_A^\ell P_Z
    \mathcal{F}_{3}^{\gamma Z}+2g_V^{\ell}g_A^{\ell}P_Z^2
    \mathcal{F}_{3}^{\gamma Z}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \mathcal{F}_{i}^{\rm CC}=\mathcal{F}_{i}^{W^\pm}\,,\\
  \end{array}
\end{equation}
where we assumed an unpolarised lepton beam, and used the definitions:
\begin{equation}
g_V^\ell=-\frac{1}{2}+2\sin^2\theta_{\rm W}\,,\quad
g_A^\ell=-\frac{1}{2}\,,\quad P_Z=\frac{G_FM_Z^2}{2\sqrt{2}\alpha}\frac{Q^2}{Q^2+M_Z^2}=\frac{1}{4\sin^2\theta_{\rm W}(1-\sin^2\theta_{\rm W})}\frac{Q^2}{Q^2+M_Z^2}\,.
\end{equation}

The general structure of the structure functions reads as follows:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{i}^{jk}&=&\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha}\mathcal{C}_{qq}^{i,jk}(\alpha)d_\alpha f_\alpha+\sum_\beta\mathcal{C}_{gq}^{i,jk}(\beta)d_g f_\beta+\sum_\alpha\mathcal{C}_{qg}^{i,jk}(\alpha)d_\alpha f_g+\mathcal{C}_{gg}^{i,jk}d_g f_g+\sum_{\alpha}\mathcal{C}_{\overline{q}q}^{i,jk}(\alpha)d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha\\
\\
&+&\displaystyle\sum_{{\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta>0\atop \alpha\neq \beta}}\mathcal{C}_{q'q}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)d_\alpha f_\beta+\sum_{{\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta<0\atop \alpha\neq-\beta}}\mathcal{C}_{\overline{q}'q}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)d_\alpha f_\beta\\
\\
&=&\displaystyle\sum_{\alpha}\left[C_{qq}^{i,jk}(\alpha)+C_{qq,\rm Fcon}^{i,jk}(\alpha)+C_{qq,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha)+C_{q'q}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\alpha)+C_{q'q, \rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\alpha)\right]d_\alpha f_\alpha\\ 
\\
&+&\displaystyle\sum_\beta\left[C_{gq}^{i,jk}(\beta)+C_{gq,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\beta)\right]d_g f_\beta+\sum_\alpha\left[C_{qg}^{i,jk}(\alpha)+C_{qg,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha)\right]d_\alpha f_g \\
\\
&+&\displaystyle\left[C_{gg}^{i,jk}+C_{gg,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}\right]d_g f_g+\sum_{\alpha}\left[C_{\overline{q}q}^{i,jk}(\alpha)+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{i,jk}(\alpha)+C_{\overline{q}'q}^{i,jk}(\overline{\alpha},\alpha)+C_{\overline{q}'q, \rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\overline{\alpha},\alpha)\right]d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha\\
\\
&+&\displaystyle\sum_{{\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta>0\atop \alpha\neq \beta}}\left[C_{q'q}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)+C_{q'q, \rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)\right]d_\alpha f_\beta+\sum_{{\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta<0\atop \alpha\neq-\beta}}\left[C_{\overline{q}'q}^{i,jk}(\overline{\alpha},\beta)+C_{\overline{q}'q, \rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\overline{\alpha},\beta)\right]d_\alpha f_\beta\,,
\end{array}
\label{eq:generalstructurefunction}
\end{equation}
where $jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ$ and the indices $\alpha$ and
$\beta$ run over quark \textit{and} antiquark. Moreover, we used the
notation $\overline{\alpha}=-\alpha$ and
$\overline{\beta}=-\beta$. The dependence on the flavour indices of
the coefficient functions $C$ for each component $jk$ factors out in
terms of appropriate charges. Sketchily,
$C_{\dots}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=A_\alpha^{i,jk}C_{\dots,\dots}^{i}$ and
$C_{\dots}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=A_{\alpha\beta}^{i,jk}C_{\dots,\dots}^{i}$.

Let us first consider the neutral-current case for $i=T,L$ which is
given by:
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal{F}_{i}^{\rm NC}=\sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}\mathcal{F}_{i}^{jk}\,,
\label{eq:FTLNC}
\end{equation}
where we have:
\begin{equation}
  \eta_{\gamma\gamma}=1\,,\quad\eta_{\gamma Z}=-g_V^\ell P_Z\,,\quad\eta_{ZZ}=(g_V^{\ell2}+g_A^{\ell2})P_Z^2\,.
\end{equation}
Given the up- and down-type quark (but not antiquark) couplings:
\begin{equation}
g_V^{d,s,b}=-\frac{1}{2}+\frac{2}{3}\sin^2\theta_{\rm W}\,,\quad g_V^{u,c,t}=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{4}{3}\sin^2\theta_{\rm W}\,,\quad g_A^{d,s,b}=-\frac{1}{2}\,,\quad g_A^{u,c,t}=\frac{1}{2}\,,
\end{equation}
which for antiquarks are $g_V^{-\alpha}=-g_V^{\alpha}$ (like the
electric change $e_{-\alpha}=-e_\alpha$) and
$g_A^{-\alpha}=g_A^{\alpha}$, the purpose is to compute:
\begin{equation}
\sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{\dots}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\dots)\,.
\end{equation}
To this end, we introduce the charges:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{l}
  \displaystyle A_{\alpha\beta}=(g_V^{\ell2}+g_A^{\ell2})g_A^\alpha g_A^\beta P_Z^2\,,\\
\\
  \displaystyle B_{\alpha\beta}=e_\alpha e_\beta-g_V^\ell(e_\alpha g_V^\beta+e_\beta g_V^\alpha)P_Z+(g_V^{\ell2}+g_A^{\ell2})g_V^\alpha g_V^\beta P_Z^2+A_{\alpha\beta}\,,
\end{array}
\end{equation}
which produce:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{l}
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{qq}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{qq}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{qq,\rm Fcon}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{i}+\left(\sum_{\gamma}B_{\gamma\gamma}\right)C_{qq,\rm Fcon,2}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{qq,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=\left(\sum_\gamma A_{\alpha\gamma}\right)C_{qq,\rm A,NoW}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{\overline{q}q}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{\overline{q}q}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{q'q}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=B_{\beta\beta}C_{q'q,1}^{i}+B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{q'q,2}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{q'q,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=(B_{\alpha\beta}-A_{\alpha\beta})C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{i}+A_{\alpha\beta}C_{q'q, \rm NoW,4}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{\overline{q}'q}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=B_{\beta\beta}C_{q'q,1}^{i}+B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{q'q,2}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{\overline{q}'q,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=(-B_{\alpha\beta}+A_{\alpha\beta})C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{i}+A_{\alpha\beta}C_{q'q, \rm NoW,4}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{gq}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{gq}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{gq,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=\left(\sum_\gamma A_{\alpha\gamma}\right)C_{gq,\rm A,NoW}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{qg}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=B_{\alpha\alpha}C_{qg}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{qg,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}(\alpha)=\left(\sum_\gamma A_{\alpha\gamma}\right)C_{qg,\rm A,NoW}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{gg}^{i,jk}=\sum_\gamma B_{\gamma\gamma}C_{gg}^{i}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\eta_{jk}C_{gg,\rm NoW}^{i,jk}=\left(\sum_{\gamma,\delta} A_{\gamma\delta}\right)C_{gg,\rm AA,NoW}^{i}\,.
  \end{array}
\end{equation}
Now, we can plug these expressions into Eq.~(\ref{eq:FTLNC}), which
finally gives:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{i}^{\rm NC}&=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{{\rm NS},i}\sum_{\alpha}B_{\alpha\alpha}d_\alpha f_\alpha+C_{gq}^{i}\sum_\beta B_{\alpha\alpha}d_g f_\beta+C_{qg}^{i}\sum_\alpha B_{\alpha\alpha}d_\alpha f_g \\ 
\\
&+&\displaystyle C_{gg}^{i}\left(\sum_\gamma B_{\gamma\gamma}\right)d_g f_g+C_{qq}^{{\rm PS},i}\left(\sum_{\gamma}B_{\gamma\gamma}\right)\sum_{\alpha}d_\alpha f_\alpha+C_{\overline{q}q}^{i}\sum_{\alpha}B_{\alpha\alpha}d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha\\
\\  
&+&\displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(1),i}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq\beta,-\beta}}B_{\beta\beta}d_\alpha f_\beta+C_{q'q}^{(2),i}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq\beta,-\beta}}B_{\alpha\alpha}d_\alpha f_\beta+C_{q'q}^{(3),i}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq\beta,-\beta}}B_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha f_\beta\\ 
\\
&+&\displaystyle \overline{C}_{qq}^{i}\sum_{\alpha}\left(\sum_\gamma A_{\alpha\gamma}\right)d_\alpha f_\alpha+\overline{C}_{gq}^{i}\sum_\beta\left(\sum_\gamma A_{\beta\gamma}\right)d_g f_\beta+\overline{C}_{qg}^{i}\sum_\alpha\left(\sum_\gamma A_{\alpha\gamma}\right)d_\alpha f_g\\ 
\\
&+&\displaystyle \overline{C}_{gg}^{i}\left(\sum_{\gamma,\delta} A_{\gamma\delta}\right)d_g f_g-C_{q'q}^{(3),i}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop\alpha\beta>0}}A_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha (f_\beta-f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{q'q}^{(4),i}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop\alpha\beta>0}}A_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha (f_\beta+f_{\overline{\beta}})\,,
\end{array}
\end{equation}
where, to align the notation with the electromagnetic case discussed
in the previous section, we defined:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{l}
    \displaystyle C_{qq}^{{\rm NS},i}= C_{qq}^{i}+C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{i}+C_{q'q,1}^{i}+C_{q'q,2}^{i}+C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{qq}^{{\rm PS},i}= C_{qq,\rm Fcon,2}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{\overline{q}q}^{i}=C_{\overline{q}q}^{i}+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{i}+C_{q'q,1}^{i}+C_{q'q,2}^{i}+C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(1),i}=C_{q'q,1}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(2),i}=C_{q'q,2}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(3),i}=C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(4),i}=C_{q'q,\rm NoW,4}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{qq}^{i}=C_{qq,\rm A,NoW}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{gq}^{i}=C_{gq,\rm A,NoW}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{qg}^{i}=C_{qg,\rm A,NoW}^{i}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{gg}^{i}=C_{gg,\rm AA,NoW}^{i}\,.
  \end{array}
\end{equation}

We can now consider the parity violating structure function
$\mathcal{F}_{3}^{\rm NC}$, which is given by:
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal{F}_{3}^{\rm NC}=\sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}\mathcal{F}_{3}^{jk}\,.
\label{eq:F3NC}
\end{equation}
with:
\begin{equation}
  \xi_{\gamma\gamma}=0\,,\quad\xi_{\gamma Z}=-g_A^\ell P_Z\,,\quad\xi_{ZZ}=2g_V^{\ell}g_A^{\ell}P_Z^2\,,
\end{equation}
We then introduce the charges:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{l}
\displaystyle D_{\alpha\beta}=-2g_A^\ell P_Ze_\alpha g_A^\beta+2g_V^{\ell}g_A^{\ell}P_Z^2 (g_A^\alpha g_V^\beta+g_V^\alpha g_A^\beta)\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle E_{\alpha\beta} = -2g_A^\ell P_Zg_A^\alpha e_\beta+4g_V^{\ell}g_A^{\ell}P_Z^2g_A^\alpha g_V^\beta\,,\\
  \\
  \displaystyle E_\beta=\sum_\alpha E_{\alpha\beta}\,.
\end{array}
\end{equation}
With these definitions at hand, we have:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{l}
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{qq}^{3,jk}(\alpha)=D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{qq}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{qq,\rm Fcon}^{3,jk}(\alpha)=D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{qq,\rm NoW}^{3,jk}(\alpha)= E_{\alpha}C_{qq,\rm A,NoW}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{\overline{q}q}^{3,jk}(\alpha)=D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{\overline{q}q}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{3,jk}(\alpha)=D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{q'q}^{3,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=D_{\beta\beta}C_{q'q,1}^{3}+D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{q'q,2}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{q'q,\rm NoW}^{3,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=D_{\beta\alpha}C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{3}+D_{\alpha\beta}C_{q'q, \rm NoW,4}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{\overline{q}'q}^{3,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=D_{\beta\beta}C_{q'q,1}^{3}-D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{q'q,2}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{\overline{q}'q,\rm NoW}^{3,jk}(\alpha,\beta)=D_{\beta\alpha}C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{3}-D_{\alpha\beta}C_{q'q, \rm NoW,4}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{gq}^{3,jk}(\alpha)=D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{gq}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{gq,\rm NoW}^{3,jk}(\alpha)= E_{\alpha}C_{gq,\rm A,NoW}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{qg}^{3,jk}(\alpha)=D_{\alpha\alpha}C_{qg}^{3}\,,\\
\\
\displaystyle \sum_{jk=\gamma\gamma,\gamma Z,ZZ}\xi_{jk}C_{qg,\rm NoW}^{3,jk}(\alpha)= E_{\alpha}C_{qg,\rm A,NoW}^{3}\,,
  \end{array}
\end{equation}
which produces:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\mathcal{F}_{3}^{\rm NC}&=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{{\rm NS},3}\sum_{\alpha}D_{\alpha\alpha}d_\alpha f_\alpha+C_{gq}^{3}\sum_\beta D_{\beta\beta}d_gf_\beta+C_{qg}^{3}\sum_\alpha D_{\alpha\alpha}d_\alpha f_g \\
  \\
&+&\displaystyle C_{\overline{q}q}^{3}\sum_{\alpha}D_{\alpha\alpha}d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha+C_{q'q}^{(1),3}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq\beta,-\beta}}D_{\beta\beta}d_\alpha f_\beta+C_{q'q}^{(2),3}\sum_{{\alpha,\beta\atop \alpha\neq\beta,-\beta}}D_{\alpha\alpha}d_\alpha f_\beta\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(3),3}\left[\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta>0}(D_{\beta\alpha}d_\alpha+D_{\beta\alpha}d_{\overline{\alpha}})f_\beta\right]+C_{q'q}^{(4),3}\left[\sum_{\alpha,\beta,\alpha\beta>0}(D_{\alpha\beta}d_\alpha-D_{\alpha\beta}d_{\overline{\alpha}})f_\beta\right]\\ 
\\
    &+&\displaystyle \overline{C}_{qq}^{3}\sum_{\alpha}E_{\alpha}d_\alpha f_\alpha+\overline{C}_{gq}^{3}\sum_\beta E_\beta d_g f_\beta+\overline{C}_{qg}^{3}\sum_\alpha E_{\alpha}d_\alpha f_g\,,
\end{array}
\end{equation}
where we have defined:
\begin{equation}
  \begin{array}{l}
    \displaystyle C_{qq}^{{\rm NS},3}= C_{qq}^{3}+C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{3}+C_{q'q,1}^{3}+C_{q'q,2}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{\overline{q}q}^{3}=C_{\overline{q}q}^{3}+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{3}+C_{q'q,1}^{3}+C_{q'q,2}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(1),3}=C_{q'q,1}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(2),3}=C_{q'q,2}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(3),3}=C_{q'q,\rm NoW,3}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle C_{q'q}^{(4),3}=C_{q'q,\rm NoW,4}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{qq}^{3}=C_{qq,\rm A,NoW}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{gq}^{3}=C_{gq,\rm A,NoW}^{3}\,,\\
    \\
    \displaystyle \overline{C}_{qg}^{3}=C_{qg,\rm A,NoW}^{3}\,.
  \end{array}
\end{equation}

We can now move to the CC structure functions characterised by the
exchange of a virtual $W$ boson, \textit{i.e} $jk=W^+W^-$. As compared
to the NC case, the ``NoW'' terms appearing in
Eq.~(\ref{eq:generalstructurefunction}) can be dropped straight away,
which significantly simplifies the general structure. However,
contrary to the NC case, CC interactions are not flavour diagonal, but
they are instead flavour changing. More specifically, for any quark
up(down)-type quark interacting with the $W$ boson, any down(up)-type
quark can be produced. The strength of the coupling is determined by
the elements of the $3\times3$ CKM matrix $V_{\alpha\beta}$, with
$\alpha\in U=\{u,c,t\}$ and $\beta\in D=\{d,s,b\}$, with $Q=D\cup
U$. Considering the case $i=T,L$ for the exchange of $W^-$, one finds:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\frac12\mathcal{F}_{i}^{W^-}
  &=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta f_\alpha+d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{gq}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2d_g(f_\alpha+f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{qg}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta+d_{\overline{\alpha}})f_g\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{gg}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2d_gf_g +C_{qq,\rm Fcon,2}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2\sum_{f\in Q}(d_ff_f+d_{\overline{f}}f_{\overline{f}})+C_{\overline{q}q}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\beta}}f_\alpha+d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\beta})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\alpha f_\alpha+d_{\overline{\beta}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha+d_{\beta}f_{\overline{\beta}})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q,1}^{i}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{f}+d_{\overline{f}})(f_\alpha+f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{q'q,2}^{i}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta+d_{\overline{\alpha}})(f_{f}+f_{\overline{f}})\,.
\end{array}
\end{equation}
The exchange of a $W^+$ is easily obtained from the expression above
by exchanging $U\leftrightarrow D$, that is:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\frac12\mathcal{F}_{i}^{W^+}
  &=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta f_\alpha+d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{gq}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2d_g(f_\alpha+f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{qg}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta+d_{\overline{\alpha}})f_g\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{gg}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2d_gf_g +C_{qq,\rm Fcon,2}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2\sum_{f\in Q}(d_ff_f+d_{\overline{f}}f_{\overline{f}})+C_{\overline{q}q}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\beta}}f_\alpha+d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\beta})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\alpha f_\alpha+d_{\overline{\beta}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{i}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha+d_{\beta}f_{\overline{\beta}})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q,1}^{i}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{f}+d_{\overline{f}})(f_\alpha+f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{q'q,2}^{i}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta+d_{\overline{\alpha}})(f_{f}+f_{\overline{f}})\,.
\end{array}
\end{equation}

We now move to considering $\mathcal{F}_{3}^{W^-}$, which reads:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\frac12\mathcal{F}_{3}^{W^-}
  &=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta f_\alpha-d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{gq}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2d_g(f_\alpha-f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{qg}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta-d_{\overline{\alpha}})f_g\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{\overline{q}q}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\beta}}f_\alpha-d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\beta})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\alpha f_\alpha-d_{\overline{\beta}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha-d_{\beta}f_{\overline{\beta}})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q,1}^{3}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{f}+d_{\overline{f}})(f_\alpha-f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{q'q,2}^{3}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in U\atop\beta\in D}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta-d_{\overline{\alpha}})(f_{f}+f_{\overline{f}})\,.
\end{array}
\end{equation}
Once again, the exchange of a $W^+$ is obtained by exchanging
$U\leftrightarrow D$:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle\frac12\mathcal{F}_{3}^{W^+}
  &=&\displaystyle C_{qq}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta f_\alpha-d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{gq}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2d_g(f_\alpha-f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{qg}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta-d_{\overline{\alpha}})f_g\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{\overline{q}q}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\beta}}f_\alpha-d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_{\beta})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{qq,\rm Fcon,1}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\alpha f_\alpha-d_{\overline{\beta}}f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{\overline{q}q,\rm Fcon}^{3}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{\overline{\alpha}}f_\alpha-d_{\beta}f_{\overline{\beta}})\\
  \\
  &+&\displaystyle C_{q'q,1}^{3}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_{f}+d_{\overline{f}})(f_\alpha-f_{\overline{\beta}})+C_{q'q,2}^{3}\sum_{f\in Q}\sum_{{\alpha\in D\atop\beta\in U}}|V_{\alpha\beta}|^2(d_\beta-d_{\overline{\alpha}})(f_{f}+f_{\overline{f}})\,.
\end{array}
\end{equation}

\subsection{Integrating over the phase space}

For implementation reasons, we take as a reference for our
calculations the cross section differential in $x$, $Q$ and $z$
integrated over the final-state phase space (bins):
\begin{equation}
  \sigma = \int_{Q_{\rm min}}^{Q_{\rm max}}dQ \int_{x_{\rm
      min}}^{x_{\rm max}}dx \int_{z_{\rm min}}^{z_{\rm
      max}}dz\frac{d^3\sigma}{dx dQdz}\,,
\label{eq:idealintegral}
\end{equation}
However, sometimes the photon invariant mass $Q$ is replaced by the
inelasticity $y$ of the process defined as in terms of the
center-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}$ as:
\begin{equation}
Q^2 = xys\,.
\end{equation}
In this case the integral over the phase space takes the form:
\begin{equation}
  \sigma = \int_{y_{\rm
      min}}^{y_{\rm max}}dy \int_{x_{\rm min}}^{x_{\rm max}}dx\int_{z_{\rm min}}^{z_{\rm
      max}}dz\frac{d^3\sigma}{dx dy dz}=\int_{\sqrt{x_{\rm min}y_{\rm min}s}}^{\sqrt{x_{\rm max}y_{\rm max}s}}dQ\int_{\overline{x}_{\rm min}}^{\overline{x}_{\rm
      max}}dx \int_{z_{\rm
      min}}^{z_{\rm max}}dz\frac{d^3\sigma}{dx dQ dz}\,,
\label{eq:lessidealintegral}
\end{equation}
with:
\begin{equation}
\overline{x}_{\rm min} = {\rm max}\left[x_{\rm min},\frac{Q^2}{sy_{\rm
    max}}\right]\quad\mbox{and}\quad \overline{x}_{\rm max} = {\rm min}\left[x_{\rm max},\frac{Q^2}{sy_{\rm
    min}}\right]\,.
\end{equation}
Often, cross sections are measured within a fiducial region defined
as:
\begin{equation}
W=\sqrt{\frac{(1-x)Q^2}{x}} \geq W_{\rm min}\,,\quad y_{\rm min} \leq
y\leq y_{\rm max}\,,\quad Q \geq Q_{\rm min}\,.
\end{equation}
These constraints have the effect of reducing the phase space of some
bins placed at the edge of the fiducial region. The net effect is that
of replacing the $x$ integration bounds in both
Eqs.~(\ref{eq:idealintegral}) and~(\ref{eq:lessidealintegral}) with:
\begin{equation}
  x_{\rm min}\rightarrow\overline{x}_{\rm min} = {\rm max}\left[x_{\rm min},\frac{Q^2}{sy_{\rm
        max}}\right]\quad\mbox{and}\quad x_{\rm max}\rightarrow\overline{x}_{\rm max} = {\rm min}\left[x_{\rm max},\frac{Q^2}{sy_{\rm
        min}},\frac{Q^2}{Q^2+W_{\rm min}^2}\right]\,.
\end{equation}

Therefore, also the integral in Eq.~(\ref{eq:lessidealintegral}) can
be recasted in the form of Eq.~(\ref{eq:idealintegral}). Using
Eq.~(\ref{eq:sidisInt}), we finally have that:
\begin{equation}
  \sigma = \sum_j
\left[\int_{z_{\rm min}}^{z_{\rm max}}dz  \left[\int_{Q_{\rm min}}^{Q_{\rm max}}dQ \left[\int_{x_{\rm min}}^{x_{\rm max}} dx\,\mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS} (z|x,Q)\right]\otimes\Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\right]\otimes d_{j}(z|Q_0)\right]\,.
\end{equation}
This expression provides the optimal structure for the implementation
in APFEL++ in terms of integrations and convolutions. Indeed, upon
integration in $x$, one finds:
\begin{equation}
\int_{x_{\rm min}}^{x_{\rm max}} dx\,\mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS} (z|x,Q)=c_i(Q;x_{\rm min},x_{\rm max})\mathbb{L}_i(z)\,,
\end{equation}
so that:
\begin{equation}
\begin{array}{rcl}
  \displaystyle \int_{Q_{\rm min}}^{Q_{\rm max}}dQ \left[\int_{x_{\rm min}}^{x_{\rm
  max}}
  dx\,\mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIDIS} (z|x,Q)\right]\otimes\Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)&=&\displaystyle \int_{Q_{\rm
                                                                 min}}^{Q_{\rm max}}dQ\,c_i(Q;x_{\rm min},x_{\rm
                                                                 max})\mathbb{L}_i(z)\otimes\Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\\
  \\
                                                             &=&\displaystyle\int_{Q_{\rm
                                                                 min}}^{Q_{\rm max}}dQ\,\mathbb{M}_j(z|x_{\rm min},x_{\rm
                                                                 max}, Q,Q_0)\\
  \\
                                                             &=&\displaystyle \mathbb{N}_j(z|x_{\rm min},x_{\rm
                                                                 max}, Q_{\rm min},Q_{\rm
                                                                 max},Q_0)
\end{array}
\end{equation}
and finally:
\begin{equation}
  \sigma = \sum_j
\int_{z_{\rm min}}^{z_{\rm max}}dz \,\mathbb{N}_j(z|x_{\rm min},x_{\rm
                                                                 max}, Q_{\rm min},Q_{\rm
                                                                 max},Q_0)\otimes d_{j}(z|Q_0)=\sum_j
\mathbb{O}_j({z_{\rm min}},{z_{\rm max}},x_{\rm min},x_{\rm
                                                                 max}, Q_{\rm min},Q_{\rm
                                                                 max},Q_0)\,.
\end{equation}

\section{Computation of the single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation
  cross section}

From the point of view of the numerical computation, the
single-inclusive $e^+e^-$ annihilation (SIA) cross section can be
regarded as a simplified version of the SIDIS one. Specifically, for
SIA the variable $x$ is just absent and there is no integration over
the scale $Q$ because $Q=\sqrt{s}$ with $\sqrt{s}$ fixed and
determined by the collision energy of the lepton pair. In addition, in
all cases considered in our analysis, data are delivered for specific
values of the variable $z$ such that no integration over $z$ is
required. Finally, the observable is computed as:
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{\sigma}\frac{d\sigma}{dz} = \sum_j
  \mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIA} (z|Q)\otimes\Gamma_{ij}(z|Q,Q_0)\otimes d_{j}(z|Q_0)\,.
\end{equation}
This equation closely resembles Eq.~(\ref{eq:sidisInt}) but the
$\mathbb{K}_{i}^{\rm SIA}$ functions have a simpler structure and, up
to a factor $\sigma_0/\sigma$, where $\sigma_0$ is the leading-order
total cross section, are already computed by APFEL up to
$\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s^2)$.
